request.system: You are an expert in clinical classification systems.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Using that structure, assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Choose the chapter letter first, then the two digits.

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient Name: [Name]
MRN: [Medical Record Number]
Admission Date: [Date]
Discharge Date: [Date]
Hospital Course: 

The patient, a 56-year-old Hispanic man, presented to the clinic with sudden-onset epigastric abdominal pain of 8/10 severity. He reported a past medical history of alcohol and cocaine abuse. During his physical examination, the patient presented with an abnormal blood glucose level and an elevated hemoglobin A1C. Computed tomography (CT) revealed abnormalities suggestive of malignancy, and elevated cancer antigen 19-9 was strongly suggestive of pancreatic carcinoma. A biopsy of the liver was performed, which showed results consistent with poorly differentiated primary pancreatic adenocarcinoma. Immunohistochemical analysis of biopsy results suggested a primary pancreaticobiliary neoplasm. 

During follow-up, the patient reported worsening left back pain, with tenderness upon palpation. A chemotherapy regimen of FOLFIRINOX was initiated. 

Overall, the patient's hospital course was notable for a diagnosis of stage IV pancreatic tail adenocarcinoma with multiple liver metastases, leading to the initiation of chemotherapy. 
Discharge Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Disposition: 

The patient was discharged from the hospital on [date]. At the time of discharge, the patient reported continued pain but was able to manage his symptoms with medication. Follow-up appointments were scheduled to reassess pain management and chemotherapy progress. 

Instructions: 

The patient was advised to continue with FOLFIRINOX chemotherapy as prescribed and to report any adverse reactions to the treatment. He was also instructed to contact his care team if his pain worsens or if he experiences new symptoms. The patient was advised to seek emergency medical attention if he experiences chest pain, shortness of breath, or other severe symptoms. 

Primary Care Provider: [Name]
Specialist: Oncology
Follow-up Appointment: [Date]

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
The principal diagnosis is the stage IV pancreatic tail adenocarcinoma, which was established during the episode and treated with chemotherapy. The category for malignant neoplasm of the pancreas is C25, and the tail is subcategory C25.2.

In ICD-10-AM, when an admission is for chemotherapy, the principal diagnosis would be Z51.1 (encounter for antineoplastic chemotherapy), with the malignancy as an additional diagnosis. Here, though, the episode included diagnostic workup (CT, liver biopsy, tumor markers) and the cancer was newly diagnosed, with chemotherapy started during the same stay. The condition chiefly responsible for the episode was therefore the pancreatic cancer itself. The liver metastases would be coded separately as C78.7, but they are secondary to the primary tumor.

CODE: C25
